items.title: Remove the orphaned packages/embed bundle

labels.name: tech_debt
labels.description: Dead code, duplicated logic, refactors

items.body:
## Problem

`packages/embed` builds a standalone `buckaroo-embed.{js,css}` bundle into
`src/tallyman_companion/static/`, but nothing loads it. The live React SPA
(`packages/app`) mounts `BuckarooServerView` from `buckaroo-js-core` directly
through its own `BuckarooEmbed` component, and the companion serves
`packages/app/dist` as a catch-all. The `static/buckaroo-embed.js` output is
never referenced by served HTML or app code.

## Evidence

- `packages/app/src/components/BuckarooEmbed.tsx:2` imports `BuckarooServerView`
  from `buckaroo-js-core` directly; it's used by `packages/app/src/pages/CatalogPage.tsx:383`
  and `packages/app/src/pages/DiffPage.tsx:176`.
- The only remaining references to the embed *output* are stale: a docstring at
  `src/tallyman_companion/buckaroo_lifecycle.py:6` and a comment at
  `.github/workflows/tests.yml:13`.
- CI builds only `packages/app` (`.github/workflows/tests.yml:53-54`);
  `packages/embed` is built nowhere.

## Removal

- Delete `packages/embed/`.
- Drop the stale docstring line at `src/tallyman_companion/buckaroo_lifecycle.py:6`.
- Drop the `packages/embed/` mention in the `.github/workflows/tests.yml` comment.
- Delete the local gitignored artifacts `src/tallyman_companion/static/buckaroo-embed.{js,css}`.

## Context

The orphaned bundle predates the SPA's switch to importing `buckaroo-js-core`
directly. The doc references (README, docs/installing.md, docs/architecture.md)
were already removed on the `docs/architecture-overview` branch.

items.title: omarchy update -y hangs on the orphaned-packages prompt

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
`omarchy update -y` blocks indefinitely at `Remove N orphaned package(s)?`. The package upgrade itself completes; the run then stops at the orphan step and waits forever.

`-y` sets `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1`, documented in `omarchy-update` as "a promise not to ask anything. Steps that would need an answer report and move on instead of waiting on a prompt nobody is here to give."

## Cause

`omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs` guards on the TTY only:

```bash
if [[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]; then
  echo "${#orphans[@]} orphaned package(s) found. Re-run omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs in a terminal to review/remove them."
  echo
  exit 0
fi

if ! gum confirm --default=false "Remove ${#orphans[@]} orphaned package(s)?"; then
```

That guard is correct when the script is called directly, but `omarchy-update` re-execs itself under `script(1)` to capture the transcript (`omarchy-update:12`):

```bash
exec env OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOGGED=1 script -qefc "$script_command" "/tmp/omarchy-update.log"
```

`script` allocates a pseudo-TTY, so `-t 0` and `-t 1` are true regardless of how the update was invoked. The guard never fires, and `gum confirm` prompts into a PTY nobody is attached to.

```console
$ bash -c '[[ -t 0 && -t 1 ]] && echo TTY || echo no-TTY' < /dev/null
no-TTY

$ script -qefc 'bash -c "[[ -t 0 && -t 1 ]] && echo TTY || echo no-TTY"' /dev/null < /dev/null
TTY
```

## Suggested fix

`omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted:74` already has the pattern:

```bash
if [[ ${OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED:-} == 1 || ! -t 0 || ! -t 2 ]]; then
```

Adding the same clause to `omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs` would fix it:

```bash
if [[ ${OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED:-} == 1 || ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]; then
```

`omarchy-update-restart` has the same shape (a bare `gum confirm` with no guard). It only prompts on a kernel change or a `reboot-required` marker so it is hit less often, but `-y` would block there too.

## Environment

- omarchy 4.0.1-1
- kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2

omarchy update deletes orphaned packages - trimming a meta-package is a trap
items.body:
Recording this because it cost a working device and the failure mode is not obvious.

## What happened

Wifi stopped working after a routine `omarchy update`. The driver loaded and
detected the chip, then could not load firmware:

```
brcmfmac: brcmf_fw_alloc_request: using brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio for chip BCM4345/6
brcmfmac mmc1:0001:1: Direct firmware load for brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.bin failed with error -2
brcmfmac: brcmf_sdio_htclk: HT Avail timeout
```

`nmcli device status` showed no `wld0` at all.

## Cause

From `/var/log/pacman.log`:

```
14:04:50  pacman -Rdd linux-firmware linux-firmware-intel linux-firmware-nvidia ...   <- the image size trim
17:15:27  pacman -Rns linux-firmware-broadcom linux-firmware-cirrus
                      linux-firmware-other linux-firmware-realtek mkinitcpio          <- omarchy update
```

The size trim removed the `linux-firmware` **meta-package**. That meta-package
was the only thing depending on `linux-firmware-broadcom` and friends, which
were still marked "installed as dependency". They became orphans.

Omarchy ships `omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs`, run on every update:

```bash
mapfile -t orphans < <(pacman -Qtdq 2>/dev/null || true)
```

so the first update after flashing deleted the wifi firmware.

## Fixed

- stage 20 marks everything in `packages/uconsole-extra.packages` as explicitly
  installed (`pacman -D --asexplicit`) and warns about remaining orphans
- `verify-image.sh` fails if the firmware packages are not explicit
- documented in `docs/02-hardware.md`

## General lesson for this repo

**Removing a meta-package orphans everything it pulled in**, and on Omarchy
orphans are deleted automatically. Any future package trimming has to re-mark
the survivors as explicit, or it becomes a delayed-action failure that shows up
only after the user updates — far from the change that caused it.

Worth auditing whenever `packages/excluded.packages` grows.

items.title: Orphaned packages left after bdep-deinit
items.body:
There are scenarios when an orphaned package can be left in the configuration after de-initializing a project it belongs to, because it has a dependent in other project initialized in the same configuration. While the orphaned packages are not invalid for `bpkg`, we should probably avoid them for `bdep`-based configurations, since there can potentially be  some operation errors later on (inability to upgrade dependencies with orphaned dependents, etc). This situation is described in the [following issue comment](https://github.com/build2/build2/issues/397#issuecomment-2184031333).

Here is the simple reproducer:

```
$ git clone https://github.com/karen-arutyunov/foo.git
$ git clone https://github.com/karen-arutyunov/fox.git

$ bdep init -C cfg @cfg -d foo/libfoo/ -- cc
$ bdep init -A cfg @cfg -d fox/libfox

$ bpkg list -pc -d cfg
dir:.../foo dir+file://.../foo
dir:.../fox dir+file://.../fox
  prerequisite git:github.com/karen-arutyunov/foo#main https://github.com/karen-arutyunov/foo.git#main

$ bpkg status -r -d cfg
!libfoo configured !1.0.0
  libbar configured 1.0.0
!libfox configured !1.0.0
  libbar configured 1.0.0

$ bdep deinit @cfg -d foo/libfoo/
deinitializing in project .../foo/
synchronizing:
  drop libfoo

$ bpkg list -pc -d cfg
dir:.../fox dir+file://.../fox
  prerequisite git:github.com/karen-arutyunov/foo#main https://github.com/karen-arutyunov/foo.git#main

$ bpkg status -r -d cfg
!libfox configured !1.0.0
  libbar configured 1.0.0

$ tree -L 1 cfg
cfg
├── build
├── buildfile
├── libbar
└── libfox
```

At this point the libbar package is orphaned. We, however, would probably want it to be re-configured, so it comes from the https://github.com/karen-arutyunov/foo.git#main repository (prerequisite of dir+file://.../fox) as if after the following additional command:

```
$ bpkg build --deorphan --plan '' --yes -d cfg ?libbar
  replace/update libbar/1.0.0
  reconfigure libfox (dependent of libbar)

$ tree -L 1 cfg
cfg
├── build
├── buildfile
├── libbar-1.0.0
└── libfox
```

items.title: Package Management: deleting a large package selection fails with "PreparedStatement can have at most 65,535 parameters"
items.body: In Software > Manage > Packages (Packages in no channel), using the header checkbox to select all packages and then clicking Delete fails with Server error, please check log files. in the Web UI. The server log shows that the deletion query is built with one bind parameter per package ID, which exceeds the hard PostgreSQL wire-protocol limit of 65,535 bind parameters per prepared statement: Caused by: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: PreparedStatement can have at most 65,535 parameters. Please consider using arrays, or splitting the query in several ones, or using COPY. Given query has 87,696 parameters The 65,535 limit is imposed by the protocol itself (the parameter count in the Bind message is a 16-bit integer), so it cannot be worked around by configuration — the query has to be chunked, or rewritten to pass the IDs as an array (= ANY(?)) instead of an IN (?, ?, ?, ...) list. This makes it impossible to clean up orphaned packages through the Web UI on servers that have accumulated a large number of them. In my case there are 94,696 orphaned packages, and the only way to remove them is to delete them in small batches. Steps to reproduce Have a server with a large number of orphaned packages (in my case ~95,000; anything above ~65,000 should trigger it, and the exact threshold depends on how many parameters are emitted per package). Navigate to Software > Manage > Packages. Select Packages in no channel in the Channel dropdown, keep Binary packages selected. Click the checkbox in the table header to select all items. The banner shows All 94696 items selected. Click Delete and confirm. The Web UI shows Server error, please check log files. and nothing is deleted.

milestone.title: Ongoing — Code health and deduplication
milestone.description: Keep the code base small, deduplicated and inside the HISS limits.

items.body:
## Problem

In application codebases (Go, Node, Rust), Praetor scans lockfiles (`go.sum`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`) and runs supply-chain scanners (e.g. `govulncheck`, `gosec`).

In workstation GitOps repositories (such as Arch Linux / CachyOS declarative workstations), packages are typically declared in flat lists (`packages/pacman.txt`, `packages/aur.txt`, `packages/flatpak.txt`) without dependency locking or cryptographic checksums.

This introduces distinct supply-chain risks for workstations:
1. **Unvetted AUR PKGBUILDs**: AUR packages execute arbitrary bash code in `PKGBUILD` scripts during build/install (`build()`, `package()`, `pre_install()`).
2. **Orphaned / Hijacked AUR Packages**: Upstream AUR packages can be abandoned, adopted by malicious actors, or deleted from AUR without notice.
3. **Rolling-Release Version Drift**: Without pinned versions or lockfiles, running package installation on a new machine or dev VM  pulls whatever latest version exists in the repository, making workstation builds non-deterministic.

## Proposed Solution

Introduce workstation package supply-chain auditing in Praetor:
1. **`praetorctl audit packages`**:

items.title: Add 'diff against last-reviewed PKGBUILD' mode to catch mid-stream hijacks
items.body:
## Idea

pkgsieve currently vets a PKGBUILD against known indicators (blocklist names, payload strings, untrusted source hosts). A PASS means "no known indicators," not "unchanged since I last trusted it."

The 2026 Atomic Arch campaign worked by **hijacking previously-legitimate, orphaned packages** and rewriting their PKGBUILDs. A package you vetted last month can turn malicious via an upstream commit you never read.

## Proposal

Add a mode that records a fingerprint (e.g. sha256) of a package's `PKGBUILD` + `*.install` + `.SRCINFO` the first time it passes, then on subsequent scans flags if those files changed since the last approval — prompting a re-review of the diff.

Sketch:
- Store approved fingerprints under `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/pkgsieve/approved/<pkgname>`.
- `pkgsieve <dir>`: if a stored fingerprint exists and differs, surface a finding and show the diff; require re-approval.
- `pkgsieve --approve <dir>`: record/update the fingerprint after a human review.
- Consider keying on the package's git HEAD when the dir is a git checkout.

## Why

Catches the exact attack vector that started this project: a trusted package quietly changing under you.

items.title: [REQUEST] Improve system stability & automatic cleanup for rolling release

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

items.body:
### Problem / Motivation

CachyOS is a powerful rolling-release distro with excellent performance, but frequent system updates sometimes break existing functionality. For example:

1. Package stability: After recent updates, core KDE apps like Spectacle developed bugs (save dialog hijacked by HEIF/AVIF plugins) that do not exist on other distros with the same Plasma version (e.g., openSUSE Tumbleweed). This suggests CachyOS-specific packaging or build configuration issues.

2. System bloat: Over time, the system accumulates large amounts of build cache, orphaned packages, and leftover files — especially for users who install from AUR. There is no built-in automatic cleanup mechanism.

CachyOS markets itself as a performance-focused, user-friendly Arch alternative. But new users (and even experienced ones) are often surprised when a routine pacman -Syu breaks screenshot tools, image viewers, or other core desktop functionality.

##Proposed Solution

1. Stability-focused update channel (optional)
   - A "stable" or "delayed" repo option that holds updates for 24-48 hours after Arch upstream, allowing critical bugs to be caught before reaching users.
   - Or a pre-update warning system if a package update is known to break common desktop workflows.

2. Built-in automatic system cleanup
   - A weekly/monthly systemd timer that safely clears:
     - Orphaned packages (pacman -Rns $(pacman -Qtdq))
     - Old package cache (pacman -Sc)
     - User app caches (thumbnails, browser cache, etc.)
     - Old build caches from ~/.cache/yay/
   - A simple GUI toggle in System Settings: "Enable automatic system cleanup"

3. Package integrity verification after updates
   - After pacman -Syu, optionally run pacman -Qk to verify no files were corrupted/missed during update.
   - Alert user if any package has missing files.

4. Better AUR build isolation
   - AUR builds currently dump everything into ~/.cache/yay/ and can leave behind multi-GB folders if interrupted (e.g., webkit2gtk build). Consider:
     - Automatic cleanup of failed/incomplete AUR builds
     - Or building in /tmp by default with automatic wipe

###  Alternatives Considered
Currently using manual workarounds:
- Custom cleanup scripts run manually
- Avoiding AUR builds when possible
- Using alternative apps (Flameshot instead of Spectacle) when CachyOS packages break
- Removing libheif and disabling kimageformats plugins manually

These workarounds are not sustainable for average users and do not address the root cause.

### Additional Context

This request is based on real-world usage experience on CachyOS with KDE Plasma 6.7.4. The system is fast and well-optimized, but the maintenance overhead is higher than it should be for a distro that targets user-friendliness.

items.title: [BUG] Global skill bundle deps list reports retained content as orphaned and contradicts prune
items.body:
## Describe the bug

APM 0.35.0 (17a2fc4) reports nested skill source folders as orphaned dependencies for a global repository-level bundle with a `skills:` selection. `apm prune` explicitly retains exactly those folders as required package content and reports a clean installation. The warning survives pruning.

Related: #2926 describes a similar problem with subdirectory dependencies on 0.30.0. This case uses a repository-level `git:` dependency and `skills:` filtering on 0.35.0.

## Environment

- macOS, zsh
- APM CLI 0.35.0 (17a2fc4), global/user scope
- lirantal/skills installed commit: `a012eae0db35adae44171563c210b425e39b6233`
- audit-ai-writing installed commit: `34d197b7e2ede7c57d11b601250b42b8a2ae303a`

## Manifest and reproduction

Relevant `~/.apm/apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: lirantal
version: 1.0.0
targets:
  - agent-skills
  - codex
  - claude
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: lirantal/skills
      skills:
        - codex-session-blogger
        - writing-style-explainer
    - jxnl/dots/agents/skills/audit-ai-writing
  mcp: []
includes: auto
scripts: {}
```

In the existing installation:

```sh
apm install -g
apm deps list -g
cd ~/.apm
apm prune
apm deps list -g
```

Actual pruning was run and produced the output below. A subsequent `apm prune --dry-run` independently reproduced the same classification. This has not yet been tested in a fresh home directory.

## Actual deps list output

Condensed table: Package | Version | Source. Each nested skill row has Skills = 1.

```text

lirantal/skills/skills/gh-bulk-pr-triage       | unknown | orphaned
lirantal/skills/skills/gh-repo-init-context    | unknown | orphaned
lirantal/skills/skills/gh-bulk-repo-edit       | unknown | orphaned
lirantal/skills/skills/codex-session-blogger   | unknown | orphaned
lirantal/skills/skills/codex-chat-organizer    | unknown | orphaned
lirantal/skills/bundles/frontend-design       | 1.0.0   | orphaned
lirantal/skills/bundles/writing               | 1.0.0   | orphaned
jxnl/dots/agents/skills/audit-ai-writing      | unknown | github

[!] 8 orphaned package(s) found (not in resolved dependency graph):
[!]   - lirantal/skills/bundles/frontend-design
[!]   - lirantal/skills/bundles/writing
[!]   - lirantal/skills/skills/codex-chat-organizer
[!]   - lirantal/skills/skills/codex-session-blogger
[!]   - lirantal/skills/skills/gh-bulk-pr-triage
[!]   - lirantal/skills/skills/gh-bulk-repo-edit
[!]   - lirantal/skills/skills/gh-repo-init-context
[!]   - lirantal/skills/skills/writing-style-explainer
[i] Run 'apm prune' to remove orphaned packages
```

The parent `lirantal/skills` dependency is missing from this table.

## Actual prune output

```text
[>] Analyzing installed packages vs apm.yml...
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/bundles/frontend-design: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/bundles/writing: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/skills/codex-chat-organizer: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/skills/codex-session-blogger: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/skills/gh-bulk-pr-triage: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/skills/gh-bulk-repo-edit: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/skills/gh-repo-init-context: required package content.
[i] Retained lirantal/skills/skills/writing-style-explainer: required package content.
[+] No orphaned packages found. apm_modules/ is clean.
```

## User-facing consequences and additional evidence

1. **Contradictory diagnostics:** `deps list` recommends cleanup that `prune` says is unnecessary and does not perform.
2. **Removed skills look installed:** editing `skills:` and running `apm install -g` correctly removed deployed copies of gh-bulk-pr-triage, gh-repo-init-context, gh-bulk-repo-edit, and codex-chat-organizer. Verified these are absent from `~/.agents/skills/`. Only codex-session-blogger and writing-style-explainer remain deployed from this repository in `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`.    Run 'apm deps list' and retry with an installed package identifier.

- Use consistent parent-owned-content rules in `deps list` and `prune`; nested source content should not become independent orphans.
- Distinguish selected/deployed skills from unselected source folders retained inside the downloaded repository.
- Recommend pruning only when content is actually eligible for pruning.
- For nested skills, explain how to edit the parent's `skills:` selection instead of suggesting an identifier uninstall rejects.
- Consider an installed commit SHA fallback when Version metadata is unavailable.

No evidence here that removed skills remain active. The confirmed defect is the listing/classification and its management guidance; retaining the full downloaded repository itself appears intentional.

items.body:
# Summary

Passing any value to `--exclude-filter` — including a package name that doesn't exist in the dependency graph — causes the entire component list to be wiped out ("`Found 0 packages`") in two situations:
1. Any solution input (`.sln`, `.slnx`, `.slnf`), with or without `--recursive` (the flag has no effect here — see root cause).
2. A single project file (`.csproj` etc.) without `--recursive`.

It works correctly only for: a single project file with `--recursive`

Reproduced on `v6.2.0` (`latest`); traced back to the commit that introduced `--exclude-filter` (#939, 1615122, 2025-04-27) — present in every release since.

## Repro

### (1) Broken: solution filter, `--recursive` has no effect either way
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MySolution.slnf --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MySolution.slnf --recursive --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`

### (2) Broken: single project, no `--recursive`
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MyProject.csproj --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`

### (3) Works: single project, with `--recursive`
  `dotnet-CycloneDX MyProject.csproj --recursive --disable-package-restore --exclude-filter "PackageThatDoesNotExist" --filename bom.json`

Cases (1) and (2) print, for every restored package:

The following orphaned packages have been removed:
    - <every single package>
  Found 0 packages

  Case (3) correctly prints `No orphaned packages were found.` and produces a full component list.

## Root cause

ExcludeFilterHelper.RemoveOrphanedPackages (ExcludeFilterHelper.cs) does a BFS starting only from packages with IsDirectReference == true, then intersects the package set with whatever's reachable:

  var queue = new Queue<DotnetDependency>(packages.Where(p => p.IsDirectReference));
  ...
  packages.IntersectWith(reachablePackages);

  This runs in Runner.cs right after packages are loaded:

  if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(options.DependencyExcludeFilter))
  {
      ExcludeFilterHelper.ExcludePackages(packages, options.DependencyExcludeFilter);
      ExcludeFilterHelper.RemoveOrphanedPackages(packages);   // ~line 251
  }

  But at this point in the flow, IsDirectReference has not been populated for most input types:

  - ProjectFileService.GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync (the method used for a plain single project without --recursive, and also used internally, per-project, by the solution path below) never sets IsDirectReference on anything.
  - ProjectFileService.RecursivelyGetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync (used only for a single project with --recursive) does set it immediately on load — this is the one path that works.
  - For .sln/.slnx/.slnf input, Runner.cs branches to SolutionFileService.GetSolutionDotnetDependencys before ever checking --recursive (Runner.cs:171-182), so the flag has no effect for solutions at all. That method does contain logic that looks like it should propagate direct-reference
  status per project:

  // SolutionFileService.cs:185-199
  var projectPackages = await _projectFileService.GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync(...);
  directReferencePackages.UnionWith(projectPackages.Where(p => p.IsDirectReference));
  ...
  foreach (var directPackage in directReferencePackages)
  {
      packages.TryGetValue(directPackage, out var package);
      package.IsDirectReference = true;
  }

  - but since GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync never sets IsDirectReference in the first place, directReferencePackages is always empty and this block is effectively dead code.
  - The only place that actually populates IsDirectReference for these paths is Runner.cs's RemoveProjectReferencesAndMakeTheirDependenciesDirect(packages) call — but that runs after the exclude-filter block (~line 344 vs ~line 251).

  So for every input type except "single project + --recursive", the BFS starts from an empty set, and the filter step deletes everything.

  Suggested fix

  Ensure IsDirectReference is populated before the exclude-filter block runs, for all input types — e.g. by moving/duplicating the RemoveProjectReferencesAndMakeTheirDependenciesDirect call (or equivalent) earlier in Runner.cs, and/or fixing GetProjectDotnetDependencysAsync to set the flag
  on load so SolutionFileService's existing propagation logic actually does something.

  Environment

  - cyclonedx-dotnet (CycloneDX global tool) 6.2.0+55877e2ae058ae9686783ac084d2257d3fcedab1
  - .NET SDK 10.0.301
  - Reproduced against a single leaf .csproj, a single .csproj with --recursive, and a multi-project .slnf

  Related

  - #445 (a related but distinct issue: --exclude-dev correctly drops top-level PrivateAssets="All" packages but leaves their transitive-only children behind as orphans)

items.title: publish-only cannot resume a partially published version
items.body:
## Summary

A `publish-only` run that is interrupted leaves the version half-published, and re-running it can never finish: `npm publish` refuses the packages that already went out, so the whole run dies on the first one.

## What happened

Version `2026.9.18-4` was prepared and tagged. A `Release` dispatch was cancelled mid-publish. Re-dispatching `publish-only` for the same version failed:

```
npm error code E403
npm error 403 Forbidden - PUT .../@code-yeongyu%2fsenpi-ai
  - You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 2026.9.18-4.
```

The registry now holds a split version:

| package | 2026.9.18-4 |
| --- | --- |
| senpi-ai | published |
| senpi-tui | published |
| senpi | missing |
| senpi-agent | missing |
| senpi-server | missing |

`@code-yeongyu/senpi` still resolves to `2026.9.18-3`, so the release is invisible to users while its version number is permanently burned.

## Expected

`publish-only` is resumable: a package already at the target version is skipped (after verifying it is the same artifact) rather than aborting the run, so an interrupted release can be completed instead of abandoned.

## Why it matters

Today the only recovery is to cut a fresh version and abandon the old number, which also leaves orphaned packages on the registry at a version nothing references.

Found while releasing RPC-host work; recovering by preparing the next version.

items.body:
### Summary

The `ansible.builtin.dnf` module currently ties `clean_requirements_on_remove` to `autoremove`, but these are not the same behavior in DNF and should be configurable independently.

Today, when removing a package with:

```yaml
- ansible.builtin.dnf:
    name: systemtap
    state: absent
```

the module does not remove dependencies, because it sets `clean_requirements_on_remove = False` unless `autoremove: true` is used.
See [dnf.py lines 165/166](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/module_utils/_embed/dnf.py#L165):
```python
    autoremove = config_dict.get('autoremove', False)
    conf.clean_requirements_on_remove = autoremove
```

But if I use:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.dnf:
    name: systemtap
    state: absent
    autoremove: true
```

The module will both set `clean_requirements_on_remove = True` AND perform `base.autoremove()`
(see [dnf.py line 630/631](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/module_utils/_embed/dnf.py#L630))
```python
            if autoremove:
                base.autoremove()
```

This makes `autoremove` broader than ‘remove this package and the dependencies made unneeded by that removal’, because it can also remove unrelated orphaned packages elsewhere on the system.

**In the current implementation:**

- conf.clean_requirements_on_remove is set from autoremove
- base.autoremove() is also called when autoremove is true

So the module effectively conflates two distinct DNF behaviors whenever you use "autoremove":

- removing a package and its newly unneeded dependencies
- performing a full autoremove/orphan cleanup

The module does not offer a way to only "remove a package and its newly unneeded dependencies" without removing ALL orphaned packages.

**Workaround used:**

I now use ansible.builtin.command: "dnf remove <package> -y"

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

dnf

### Additional Information

A separate option such as:

```yaml
- ansible.builtin.dnf:
    name: package_name
    state: absent
    clean_requirements_on_remove: true
```

would make it possible to remove a package and the dependencies made unneeded by that removal, without triggering a full `autoremove` sweep.

This would provide a more precise behavior that matches DNF’s `clean_requirements_on_remove` setting, while preserving the current broader behavior of `autoremove: true`.

items.body:
## What it is

Julia keeps packages, downloaded artefacts, repository clones and precompiled images in one depot,
`%USERPROFILE%\.julia` by default, with `JULIA_DEPOT_PATH` overriding it. The depot's children are
documented:

| Child | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `packages` | Installed package source, explicit and implicit alike |
| `artifacts` | Content packages depend on, which Pkg installs for them |
| `clones` | Full clones of package repositories |
| `compiled` | Precompiled `.ji` images |
| `scratchspaces` | Package-managed scratch storage |

Julia ships the eviction command, and it is unusually well-suited to this product:

```julia
Pkg.gc()                            # orphaned packages, artefacts and scratch spaces
Pkg.gc(collect_delay = Day(0))      # without the default seven-day grace period
```

`Pkg.gc()` sweeps every known manifest, works out what no project references any more, and removes
only what has been unused for `collect_delay`, which defaults to seven days. That is the same idea as
the age filter already in the product, implemented by the tool itself.

## Evidence

**Researched, not measured.** Julia is not installed on the machine this survey was taken from.

## Proposed scope

**Tier 2**, command-first under §5.1. `Pkg.gc()` is strictly better than any path rule Deguffer could
write, because it knows which projects still reference what and a directory listing does not.

**Never** the depot root, `environments` (the user's own project environments), `config`,
`registries` or `logs`. This is §5.2: `%USERPROFILE%\.julia` is a tool root with configuration in it.

Sources: [Julia environment variables](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/manual/environment-variables/),
[Pkg.jl API, Pkg.gc](https://pkgdocs.julialang.org/v1/api/),
[Pkg.jl depots](https://pkgdocs.julialang.org/dev/depots/).

## Basilisk Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Project Foundation
1. Initialize Rust project with `cargo init`
2. Set up `Cargo.toml` with dependencies:
   - `pyo3` (Python bridge)
   - `tokio` + `reqwest` (async downloads)
   - `rusqlite` (SQLite)
   - `blake3` (hashing)
   - `zstd` (compression)
   - `ed25519-dalek` (signatures)
   - `anyhow`, `thiserror` (error handling)
   - `clap` (CLI)
   - `tempfile`, `pathdiff`, `num_cpus`

### Phase 2: Core Engine Modules
```
src/
├── main.rs           # CLI entry point (clap)
├── lib.rs            # PyO3 module export
├── engine/
│   ├── context.rs    # BuildContext, CommandBuilder, DependencyInfo
│   ├── sandbox.rs    # macOS Seatbelt sandbox wrapper
│   └── rpath.rs      # Mach-O RPATH relocation
├── state/
│   ├── database.rs   # SQLite operations
│   └── schema.rs     # Tables: packages, major_links, dependencies
├── resolver/
│   └── sat.rs        # SAT solver (pubgrub algorithm)
├── storage/
│   ├── bottle.rs     # .tar.zst extraction & metadata
│   └── links.rs      # Major symlink management
├── downloader/
│   └── fetch.rs      # Async bottle downloader
└── crypto/
    └── verify.rs     # Ed25519 signature verification
```

### Phase 3: CLI Commands
- `bsk install <pkg@major>` - Install with auto-resolve
- `bsk list --links` - Show major symlink mappings
- `bsk gc` - Garbage collect orphaned packages
- `bsk doctor` - Verify RPATH integrity
- `bsk uninstall <pkg>` - Remove package
- `bsk search <query>` - Search available packages

### Phase 4: Recipe System (PyO3 Bridge)
- Python `basilisk_engine` module with `BuildContext`, `CommandBuilder`
- Recipe base class for `basilisk-mpm/recipes`
- Sandboxed recipe execution

### Phase 5: Bottle Infrastructure
- GitHub Actions CI/CD for building bottles
- Ed25519 signing pipeline
- METADATA.json schema validation

## Summary

A workspace-level scan found 12 packages under `packages/*` with zero inbound references outside their own directory after excluding `node_modules`, build output, `.omc`, `reference/**`, and `bun.lock`.

## Orphaned packages

- `packages/adaptive-loadout` (`@harness/adaptive-loadout`)
- `packages/api-generator` (`@harness/api-generator`)
- `packages/config-optimizer` (`@harness/config-optimizer`)
- `packages/figma-integration` (`@harness/figma-integration`)
- `packages/fixed-boundary` (`@rfs/fixed-boundary`)
- `packages/implementation-loop` (`@rfs/implementation-loop`)
- `packages/knowledge` (`@harness/knowledge`)
- `packages/schema-generator` (`@harness/schema-generator`)
- `packages/secret-manager` (`@harness/secret-manager`)
- `packages/sentry-integration` (`@harness/sentry-integration`)
- `packages/status-dashboard` (`@harness/status-dashboard`)
- `packages/task-classifier` (`@rfs/task-classifier`)

## Evidence

- The root workspace includes every package via [`package.json`](https://github.com/Cheggin/request-for-startups/blob/main/package.json) `workspaces: ["packages/*"]`.
- The root test script iterates every package directory via `test:all`, so even unintegrated packages stay in the install / test surface.
- A repo-wide reference scan for each package name returns no callers outside the package itself once `bun.lock`, `node_modules`, build output, and `reference/**` are excluded.

## Why this matters

- Dead packages increase maintenance cost and install / test noise.
- They make it unclear which packages are actually part of the shipped harness.
- They hide ownership gaps because unfinished experiments look like supported modules.

## Suggested fix

For each package, do one of the following:

1. Wire it into the CLI / runtime / docs as a supported package.
2. Move it to an incubator or `reference/` area if it is experimental.
3. Delete or archive it if it is abandoned.

Also add a repo check that flags workspace packages with zero inbound references.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each listed package is either integrated, relocated out of `packages/*`, or removed.
- The workspace only includes packages with an active runtime / CLI / docs path.
- CI includes a lightweight orphan-package detector so this does not regress.

items.title: [BUG] Deployed files of a dependency removed upstream are orphaned after `git pull`: `audit`, `install` and `prune` all miss them

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something does not work as documented.

labels.name: triage/recommended
labels.description: Automated advice completed; not human scope approval.

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a dependency is removed from `apm.yml` on one machine and the updated `apm.yml` / `apm.lock.yaml` reach a teammate through `git pull`, the teammate's deployed files for that dependency (e.g. `.claude/skills/<name>/`) are never cleaned up, and nothing reports them:

- `apm audit --ci` passes all checks, including `drift`. The docs list "orphan files left after their source was removed" as one of the failure modes drift detection catches (`orphaned`), but the replay starts from the new lockfile, which no longer mentions the dependency. The code itself disagrees on what `orphaned` means: the [module docstring](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/280b8a7b115b7a0c9b232467c376480c7cfde04e/src/apm_cli/install/drift.py#L9-L10) defines it as a file "not present in the scratch replay AND not tracked in the lockfile", while the [implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/280b8a7b115b7a0c9b232467c376480c7cfde04e/src/apm_cli/install/drift.py#L1006-L1018) only reports files that *are* tracked in the current lockfile and skips untracked ones as user-authored. The docstring's definition would cover this case; the implementation does not.
- `apm install` does not remove them. On the author's machine the same install cleans them up ("2 stale files cleaned"), because the previous lockfile still recorded them as `deployed_files`. On the teammate's machine that record was overwritten by the pull before any APM command ran.
- `apm prune` detects the orphaned package and removes `apm_modules/_local/<name>`, but leaves its deployed files in place. After that, the package source is gone too, so APM has no remaining way to attribute those files.

As a result, the removed skill stays active for the teammate's agent indefinitely, and every check says the workspace is clean.

This is the common setup where `apm_modules/` and the deployed directories are gitignored and only `apm.yml` + `apm.lock.yaml` are committed.

**To Reproduce**

Self-contained script. It uses two local dependencies for portability; the mechanism only depends on the lockfile being replaced by `git pull`.

```sh
set -e
W="$(mktemp -d)" && cd "$W"

# author: project with two local dependencies, each shipping one skill
mkdir author && cd author && git init -q
for p in alpha beta; do
  mkdir -p "pkgs/$p/.apm/skills/$p"
  printf 'name: %s\nversion: 1.0.0\n' "$p" > "pkgs/$p/apm.yml"
  printf -- '---\nname: %s\ndescription: Demo %s\n---\n\nBody.\n' "$p" "$p" > "pkgs/$p/.apm/skills/$p/SKILL.md"
done
printf 'name: demo\nversion: 1.0.0\ntargets:\n  - claude\ndependencies:\n  apm:\n    - ./pkgs/alpha\n    - ./pkgs/beta\n' > apm.yml
printf 'apm_modules/\n.claude/\n' > .gitignore   # deployed files are not committed
apm install
git add -A && git -c user.name=a -c user.email=a@a commit -qm "add alpha and beta"

# teammate clones and installs
cd .. && git clone -q author teammate && (cd teammate && apm install)

# author drops beta
cd author
sed -i.bak '/pkgs\/beta/d' apm.yml && rm apm.yml.bak
apm install          # author's copy: "2 stale files cleaned"
git -c user.name=a -c user.email=a@a commit -qam "drop beta"

# teammate pulls
cd ../teammate && git pull -q
apm audit --ci --no-policy   # passes
apm install                  # does not remove .claude/skills/beta
apm prune                    # removes apm_modules/_local/beta only
ls .claude/skills            # alpha  beta
```

**Expected behavior**

In order of importance:

1. `apm audit` reports `.claude/skills/beta/**` as `orphaned` drift (and `--ci` fails), as documented.
2. `apm install` removes the deployed files of a package that left the resolved graph, the same way it already does when the previous lockfile is available locally. Attribution is still possible on the teammate's machine: `apm_modules/_local/beta` is present, so APM can recompute what that package deploys and delete only files whose bytes still match. Files the user edited are kept and reported, consistent with how #2292 preserves user-edited bytes.
3. `apm prune` does not discard `apm_modules/<pkg>` while that package's deployed files remain. It either cleans them in the same operation or leaves the package in place and reports the files.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.3.0, arm64)
 - Python Version: N/A (standalone release binary)
 - APM Version: 0.33.0 (18c4c43); also reproduces on 0.29.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**

Teammate side, after `git pull`:

```
### apm audit --ci --no-policy
[>] Replaying install (cache-only)...
[+] Replayed 1 package(s)
[>] Diffing scratch vs working tree...
[+] No drift detected
...
│ [+]      │ deployed-files-present   │ All deployed files present on disk     │
│ [+]      │ no-orphaned-packages     │ No orphaned packages in lockfile       │
│ [+]      │ drift                    │ no drift detected against lockfile     │
[*] All 10 check(s) passed

### apm install
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[i] Targets: claude  (source: apm.yml)
  [+] ./pkgs/alpha (local)
  |-- 1 skill(s) integrated -> .claude/skills/
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.1s.

### apm prune
[>] Analyzing installed packages vs apm.yml...
[!] Found 1 orphaned package(s):
[!]   - _local/beta
[i] Removed _local/beta
[*] Pruned 1 orphaned package(s)

### ls .claude/skills
alpha
beta
```

Author side, same change, for comparison:

```
[i] Cleaned 2 files from packages no longer in apm.yml
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency (2 stale files cleaned) in 0.1s.
```

**Additional context**

- Root cause as observed: deployment ownership lives only in `apm.lock.yaml`. In a team, the lockfile is a shared, version-controlled file, so it can be replaced underneath a working tree by `git pull`, `git checkout` or a merge. Cleanup that depends on diffing the previous lockfile against the new one only works on the machine that made the change.
- Scope check: with the same script but only `apm_modules/` gitignored (deployed files committed), the issue does not occur. The author's `apm install` deletes `.claude/skills/beta/SKILL.md`, that deletion is committed, and `git pull` removes it on the teammate's side. So this only affects projects that gitignore deployed outputs. That remains a supported repository choice (#1342 was closed as not planned, leaving commit-vs-ignore to each repository), so APM needs to handle it.
- `apm prune --dry-run` does flag `_local/beta` before `apm prune` runs. That signal disappears after the first prune.
- Related but distinct: #3179 (local `.apm/` skills not cleaned from `.agents/skills/` on the same machine), #2292 (prune reconciling ledger ownership when the lock still knows the departed owner), #2296 / #2304 (`apm lock` deferring deletion to the next install).

items.title: PB-009 — Implement PacmanAdapter (all methods, RC-02, RC-10)

labels.name: foundation
labels.description: Repository, project structure, core scaffolding, and foundational work.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Description

Implement the pacman adapter for Arch-family distributions (Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS,
Garuda, Artix). This adapter carries the two risk flags assigned to the package layer:

- **RC-02** — `checkupdates` lives in `pacman-contrib` and is not always installed, so the
  adapter must detect its absence and fall back gracefully.
- **RC-10** — `pacman -Rns $(pacman -Qdtq)` fails when no orphans exist, so the adapter must
  check for orphans before attempting removal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `kommand/adapters/pacman.py` defines `PacmanAdapter`, subclassing
      `PackageManagerAdapter`
- [ ] `name = "pacman"` and `distro_ids` covers the Arch-family IDs routed in
      `ADAPTER_MAP` (`arch`, `manjaro`, `endeavouros`, `garuda`, `artix`)
- [ ] **RC-02:** `check_updates()` uses `checkupdates` when it is present
- [ ] **RC-02:** when `checkupdates` is absent, the adapter falls back to syncing with
      `pacman -Sy --noconfirm` and listing upgradable packages with `pacman -Qu`, without
      raising and without prompting the user interactively
- [ ] **RC-02:** exit code 2 from `checkupdates` (no updates available) is treated as
      success with an empty list, not as an error
- [ ] The parser handles the `name current-version -> new-version` format and ignores
      malformed lines
- [ ] `check_updates()` never raises — any failure returns an empty list and records
      technical detail for the log
- [ ] **RC-10:** `autoremove()` queries orphans with `pacman -Qdtq` **before** attempting
      removal
- [ ] **RC-10:** when no orphans exist, `autoremove()` yields a single completed
      `CommandResult` stating no orphaned packages were found, with exit code 0, and does
      **not** invoke `pacman -Rns`
- [ ] **RC-10:** when orphans exist, `autoremove()` streams `pacman -Rns --noconfirm` with
      the orphaned package names as separate arguments
- [ ] `upgrade()` streams `pacman -Syu --noconfirm` as `CommandResult` chunks, ending with
      `is_complete=True` and the real `exit_code`
- [ ] `clean_cache()` streams `pacman -Sc --noconfirm`
- [ ] `list_installed()` returns explicitly installed packages as `PackageInfo` entries
- [ ] `reboot_required()` compares the running kernel version with the installed kernel
      package version and never raises
- [ ] Every subprocess call uses `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` with an argument list —
      no `shell=True` and no shell command substitution
- [ ] Both RC-02 paths and both RC-10 paths are covered by unit tests in PB-022

**Out of scope:** `install()` and `remove()` (v2.0) and automatically installing
`pacman-contrib` — the fallback path exists precisely so Kommand does not need to.
